text:
Diego Ramos: Sedgewell submitted their vendor questionnaire during onboarding. Key asks: confirm encryption at rest + key custody options, SOC2 status, subprocessors list & DPA redline stance, and embeddings retention policy. Posting their exact bullets below.

Diego Ramos: ```
1) Is customer data encrypted at rest? Who manages keys and is BYOK available?
2) Provide SOC2 report or timeline for completion.
3) List of subprocessors and process for changes. Will you accept our DPA edits?
4) How long do you retain embeddings and can we request deletion?
```

Aisha Khan: Short answers for customer email: "Yes. All data at rest is encrypted. Hosted customers use cloud KMS (AWS/GCP) with envelope encryption; Dedicated/Private supports customer-managed keys (BYOK). HSM-backed options available on request. Key access is role-based and logged."

Diego Ramos: Nice. Can you add a one-liner about key separation for multi-tenant hosted customers? They asked specifically about separating tenant keys.

Aisha Khan: Add: "For Hosted customers we use service-side CMKs; we can offer key separation via dedicated CMKs for customers on Dedicated plans or via BYOK for eligible customers."

Ben Cooper: For the SOC2 item: we are SOC2 in-progress. Type II expected by 2025-09-30. We can share the SOC2 readiness pack (control mapping, test plan, interim evidence) now under NDA. Final report will be shared under NDA once issued. Tagging Legal for any DPA redlines.

Diego Ramos: Good. Customer also wants a current subprocessors list and to know how we notify changes. What do we normally do?

Aisha Khan: We publish the current subprocessors in the Trust Center (link: https://redwood.example.com/trust/subprocessors) and send 30 days' notice by email for material changes. We do not require prior written consent for routine infra changes; we include an objection window.

Ben Cooper: DPA redlines: we accept reasonable edits but will not accept open-ended flow-downs or open liability increases. Suggest we offer our standard DPA + subprocessors appendix; if the customer returns aggressive redlines, route to Legal for review (that's me).

DeployBot: Note: attach SOC2 readiness pack and subprocessors export when replying.

Diego Ramos: They also asked about embeddings retention and deletion API. We do store embeddings for X days by default?

Aisha Khan: Current policy: embeddings retention default = 365 days for hosted, configurable for Dedicated/Private. We support on-demand deletion requests via support ticket and can run a one-time purge for data subject requests. Include link to retention policy: https://redwood.example.com/docs/data-retention.

Ben Cooper: Suggested reply snippet (customer-facing): "We encrypt all customer data at rest. Hosted customers use cloud KMS with envelope encryption; Dedicated/Private supports BYOK and HSM-backed keys. We are completing SOC2 Type II (expected 2025-09-30) and can provide a readiness pack under NDA. Our standard DPA includes a subprocessors appendix and we provide 30 days' notice before changes; Legal will review any non-standard redlines."

Diego Ramos: Perfect. I'll draft an email with Aisha's key separation line + Ben's DPA snippet + links. Flagging Legal on the send. Planning to respond within 24h.

OnboardingBot: Reminder set  Reply to Sedgewell questionnaire within 24h.

Aisha Khan: I can attach the KMS diagram and retention policy. Diego, ping me if they request HSM vendor certification and I'll pull certs.

Ben Cooper: I'll standby for any redlines. If they push deletion SLA <30 days or broad subprocessors consent, escalate to me.

Diego Ramos: Thanks all. Will share the sent message here once I hit send. :email:
